monthly_review.summary: Performance this month shows modest volume and intensity consistency, but notable pacing variability and underutilization of Zone 1 recovery work. Aerobic efficiency improved slightly while cadence remained stable.
monthly_review.highlight: The most notable finding is the complete absence of logged runs this month — all 44 lifetime runs occurred before April 30, meaning zero running activity has been recorded in May 2026 so far.

goal_tracker.message: You need 38.0 more km across 9 sessions to match last month’s volume. With 31 days remaining, that averages to ~1.2 km/day or 4.3 km every 3 days — very achievable with just 2–3 short runs per week.

insights.title: Efficiency increased despite pace variability
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose to 13.66 km/hr per bpm last month — up from an implied baseline (given VO2 max stability at 35–36), suggesting better oxygen utilization per heartbeat, likely aided by recent faster efforts like the 7:13/km run on 4/22.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominates training load, limiting recovery and endurance foundation
insights.body: Zone 3 accounts for 26% of HR time — higher than Zones 1 (23%) and 2 (32%) combined — indicating frequent 'moderately hard' efforts without sufficient low-Z1 recovery (only 23%) or true Z2 aerobic base building (32%).

insights.title: Cadence-pacing disconnect reveals form stress at slow speeds
insights.body: On 4/26, cadence dropped sharply to 87 spm at 14:00/km (840 sec/km) — a 40% reduction from typical 146–150 spm — suggesting compromised stride mechanics, possibly due to fatigue, low motivation, or walking intervals not captured in data.

insights.title: High-intensity exposure remains low but consistent
insights.body: Zone 4 (15%) and Zone 5 (4%) together make up 19% of HR time — aligning with a balanced weekly structure (e.g., one threshold + one short VO2 session), though Zone 5 is at the lower end of effective stimulus for VO2 adaptation.

recommendations.action: Do a 5km Zone 1 run (HR ≤125 bpm) within next 48 hours, using your 4/26 effort (120 bpm, 14:00/km) as a pacing reference — focus on maintaining ≥135 spm even at slow pace.
recommendations.reason: Your lowest HR run (4/26) shows Zone 1 is accessible but cadence collapsed; rebuilding neuromuscular rhythm at low intensity will reinforce aerobic efficiency and reduce vertical oscillation drift.

recommendations.action: Replace one mid-week run with a 20-min Zone 2 tempo (HR 130–138 bpm) at steady 8:45/km (525 sec/km), matching your 4/28 pace and HR (132 bpm, 8:44/km).
recommendations.reason: This targets your dominant Zone 2 window (32% of time) while bridging the gap between easy and threshold — improving lactate clearance without overloading recovery.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 × 3-min progressive stride drill post-run this week: start at 145 spm, increase by 5 spm each rep, focusing on landing under center of mass (reduce ground contact time from current avg 309 ms).
recommendations.reason: Your average ground contact time (309 ms) and vertical oscillation (7.8 cm) are elevated vs elite recreational norms; targeted neuromuscular work improves stride efficiency without added volume.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish neural control at low intensities, rebuild cadence consistency across paces, and intentionally activate Zone 1 physiology to reset autonomic balance after recent mixed-intensity efforts.
suggested_sessions: Zone 1 Foundation Run (5km, HR ≤125 bpm, cadence ≥135 spm)
Zone 2 Tempo Run (20 min, HR 130–138 bpm, pace ~8:45/km)
Strides + Form Drills (3 × 3-min progressive cadence drills post-run)
